bull_bear.body:
- Became completely debt-free during the year by monetising land/property assets, freeing balance-sheet capacity for reinvestment
- Diversified a large single-stock (Hero MotoCorp) treasury holding into multiple asset classes (stocks, mutual funds, AIFs, FDs) to reduce concentration risk and volatility
- Long-tenured promoter/executive leadership (Chairman & MD since 1999, over 47 years of industrial operating experience) providing continuity and deal execution track record on the Noida/Greater Noida asset sales
- Disciplined capital-deployment stance -- management explicitly waits for adequate margin of safety in real estate rather than chasing high valuations/low yields
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Currency risk on treasury holdings — Management identifies INR depreciation as the largest risk to the Company's treasury portfolio; existing hedges (small investments in global-stock funds, gold/silver exposure) are considered likely insufficient to offset this.
- Market/investment volatility in treasury operations — Since diversifying out of its long-term Hero MotoCorp holding into stocks, mutual funds, AIFs and FDs, the Company is exposed to market shocks (e.g. the US/Israel-Iran conflict caused negative March returns after 11 otherwise good months); management expects volatility to persist episodically even if returns normalise over the longer term.
- Real estate sector concentration and cyclicality — The Company's historical business and remaining strategy are tied to Indian (Noida/NCR) commercial and industrial real estate, exposing it to sectoral valuation cycles, rental yield compression and local regulatory/bye-law complexity.
- Oversupply risk in Noida office market — Management flags that the large number of upcoming properties on the Noida-Greater Noida Expressway will likely lead to renewed over-supply in that office market, a risk relevant to any future re-entry into the segment.
- General economic, regulatory and taxation risk — The Company discloses exposure to economic, regulatory, taxation and environmental risks, as well as sectoral investment outlook risk, as part of its normal course of business.
- Credit, liquidity, counterparty and commodity-inflation risk — Board's risk outlook explicitly lists credit risk, liquidity risk, counterparty risk, regulatory risk, commodity inflation risk and market risk as risks that could affect the Company's ability to address future developments.
- Global macro and geopolitical disruption — MD&A cites trade tariffs, USA-Europe/Venezuela/Iran-Israel/India-Pakistan/Israel-Lebanon/Russia-Ukraine tensions and Strait of Hormuz supply-chain disruption as sources of inflation, currency weakening and broader market uncertainty that can affect the Company's investment and business environment.

business.body: The Company operates in facility management services and leasing of owned property, and in the purchase, acquisition, building and construction of property, historically concentrated in Noida and New Delhi commercial/industrial real estate. Following the sale of its Knowledge Boulevard commercial asset and its Greater Noida industrial land, and the divestment of its subsidiary Emirates Technologies Private Limited, the Company is now largely a treasury operation, parking surplus capital in debt mutual funds, equities/mutual funds/AIFs/FDs while it searches for new real-estate opportunities at favourable valuations. It was previously a manufacturer of Hero Majestic Mopeds before its transformation into a commercial real estate player.

- Diversified a large single-stock (Hero MotoCorp) treasury holding into multiple asset classes (stocks, mutual funds, AIFs, FDs) to reduce concentration risk and volatility
- Long-tenured promoter/executive leadership (Chairman & MD since 1999, over 47 years of industrial operating experience) providing continuity and deal execution track record on the Noida/Greater Noida asset sales
- Disciplined capital-deployment stance -- management explicitly waits for adequate margin of safety in real estate rather than chasing high valuations/low yields
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Utilise borrowed funds only to enhance return on equity in rental-yielding commercial real estate assets and to look for higher-yield asset opportunities, having become debt-free
- Continue diversified treasury operations (stocks, mutual funds, AIFs, FDs) rather than concentrating capital in a single holding, to reduce volatility while pursuing growth
- Consider purchase of more real estate assets for investment and growth as favourable opportunities arise, while patiently waiting given currently high valuations and low yields
- Strengthen and diversify the advisor/consultant base (Finance, Business Development, Project Management, Marketing, IT, Hospitality) to enhance domain capability while keeping fixed costs low
- The Board's stated capital-management objective is to safeguard the Company's ability to continue as a going concern while maintaining an optimal capital structure to reduce the cost of capital, adjusting dividends, returning capital to shareholders, or issuing new shares as conditions warrant. Following the monetisation of real-estate/industrial assets and the sale of its stake in ETPL, the Company became debt-free and paid a substantial dividend (a special interim dividend plus a proposed final dividend), with management indicating further dividends will be considered as cashflows allow, while surplus capital is meanwhile deployed into diversified treasury investments (debt mutual funds, equities, AIFs, FDs) pending fresh real-estate opportunities at favourable valuations.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 the Company divested rather than expanded: it exited the Knowledge Boulevard commercial office asset in Noida and sold its large industrial land parcel in Greater Noida, both at what management describes as favourable valuations, and sold its entire 80% stake in subsidiary Emirates Technologies Private Limited (ETPL) on September 4, 2025. No new plant, capacity addition, or named capex project is disclosed; management states it is now searching for new real-estate opportunities but is deferring purchases because it currently finds high valuations and low yields, preferring to wait for better margin of safety.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Real estate has generally done well with steady interest rates, rising prices and increased deal activity; office space demand saw robust growth
- Residential real estate saw strong growth in the past couple of years and is now stabilising, driven by urbanisation, shifting demographics, aspirational lifestyle and economic growth
- Robust growth in leasing/occupancy and a significant uptick in property values allowed the Company to liquidate assets at prices favourable versus rental yield, eliminating debt and creating reinvestment capacity
- Risk of over-supply in Noida office space from the sheer number of upcoming properties on the Noida-Greater Noida Expressway
- High valuations and low yields, plus long project timeframes and complex local bye-laws, are making it hard to find new real-estate opportunities with adequate margin of safety, so management is waiting for more attractive prices
- Treasury returns are subject to market volatility (e.g. the US/Israel-Iran shock hit March returns after 11 otherwise good months); management expects this volatility to be temporary and returns to normalise over the longer term
- INR depreciation is viewed as the largest treasury risk; existing hedges (small global-stock funds, gold/silver) are seen as insufficient

deepdive.thesis: Majestic Auto Limited is a Delhi-NCR commercial real-estate and facility-management company that has monetised its Noida/Greater Noida property assets and become debt-free, now redeploying capital into diversified treasury investments (equities, mutual funds, AIFs, FDs) while it waits for attractively priced real-estate opportunities.

open.item: Board proposed a Final Dividend of Rs. 25 per share for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM.
Company to consider purchase of more real estate assets for investment and growth as favourable opportunities arise, having exited its Noida/Greater Noida holdings.

Company intends to continue treasury operations diversified across debt mutual funds, equities, mutual funds and AIFs, aiming to grow surplus capital at a reasonable pace with reduced single-stock concentration risk.
Management flags INR depreciation as the largest risk to the treasury portfolio, noting that current equity/gold hedges may be insufficient.
Company's stated goal is to utilise borrowed funds only to enhance return on equity in its rental-yielding commercial real estate assets and to pursue higher-yield asset opportunities.
Management flags that the sheer number of upcoming properties on the Noida-Greater Noida Expressway will soon lead to over-supply again in that office market.
Following a substantial dividend paid last year on shareholder feedback, the company will consider another dividend again as cashflows allow, and is striving to improve this position.

Company is strengthening and diversifying its advisors and consultants across Finance, Business Development, Project Management/execution, Marketing, IT and Hospitality, while keeping fixed costs low.
